title: Chinese manufacturing import penetration and firm performance: evidence from Belt and Road Initiative countries
summary: The paper examines how Chinese manufacturing import penetration affects the performance of manufacturing firms in Belt and Road Initiative countries. Chinese imports crowd out firms' productive capacity while acting as a catalyst for their internationalisation.
keyFindings: Chinese imports reduce productivity growth and employment, while firms' export capabilities rise.
Innovation and foreign licensing significantly moderate the adverse effects.
The effects are significant in middle-income countries and among small and medium-sized enterprises.
methods: World Bank Enterprise Survey firm data combined with UN Comtrade industry data for 59 BRI countries, 2011–2020, using a multi-level modelling approach.
